items.title: First time court appearance: What not to do
items.summary: We all carry our fair share of courtroom mishaps, particularly from the early years. While mistakes can happen at any stage of the litigation career, the shaking and trembling hits very differently to the newly robed, often accompanied by a strong conviction that the legal career is over and it’s time to relocate to another country. To celebrate these mandatory rites of passage, I polled my litigation circle and discovered these gems. 1. During my first year, I was sent to seek a simple passover before a Supreme Court bench with clear instructions to say “my senior is on his legs in another courtroom”. But of course, appearing before a Supreme Court bench, my overwhelm got the better of me and being painfully honest, I blurted out, “my senior is on his legs in the NCLT” . At this point, I was not aware of the unwritten rule of forum hierarchy. I got a well-deserved chewing out from my senior at this point. - 23 y/o advocate assisting a well sought after criminal lawyer in Delhi. 2.
